label: The rule
title: The Gump Rule
blurb: What the automaton is: the twelve faces each face watches, the planes nothing is ever born across, and the chaotic state a box fills with.
connects: The walls are why every closed box ends; how it ends is the next page.

label: How faces die
title: How Gump Faces Die
blurb: A box of chaos ends one whole face at a time. The staircase of deaths, one face of a box dying up close, two ways to die (a wrapped face crashes, a face of a box fades), and whether a death is luck or lineage.
connects: How long a face lasts, as a function of its size and shape, is the area law.

plates.v: Whole faces of a box die, one at a time
A face of a box: busy, then gone in ten generations
A face of a box: a dip that keeps going; at the end a loose knot, not a dense core
A wrapped face over-fills and crashes; a face of a box fades; its rim row is why. No price follows
Waits are memoryless; faces do not age

label: The area law
title: The Gump Area Law
blurb: A face's lifetime grows exponentially with its area. The price per cell, and what else counts: width, the shortest way round a wrapped face, symmetry.
connects: What is left when the last face dies is debris, the next page.

Twisted faces: equal area, different lifetimes

label: Debris and clocks
title: Gump Debris and Clocks
blurb: What a dead box leaves behind: still lifes, clocks whose period is twist times loop, a compound clock, wires, and the lives that settle unrecognised.
connects: Wires carry pulses: signals are the next page.

plates.v: Period = twist × loop; a 4 × 13 compound; wires
4 in a million settle unseen; bounded; most are wires

label: Signals
title: Gump Signals
blurb: Pulses that travel along wires, a gate, a clock of any length, a gun, an echo, the meetings of signals, run live on this page; a line that turns itself into a register, and a memory cell that pulses write and a call reads out, also live; what still does not listen; and how much of its state space a seed ever visits.
connects: Gump is one rule among many; its relatives are the next page.

plates.v: Pulses on wires; a gate; a clock of any length
Fifteen cells write a rake onto a wire every 4 generations
plates.st: three codes; proved at every length
